Subject: TTFT & streaming requirements — post-call recap

Thanks again for the time today, Alex — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we’re aligned on TTFT / streaming SLOs and what we need to validate:

TL;DR: BlinkHealth target = <= 300ms TTFT for lookups (95th), streaming responses for multi-sentence explanations (SSE or WebSocket) with chunk cadence ~150–300ms, sustained throughput target ~200 QPS, burst concurrency up to 80.

What we heard during the call:
- Primary flow: short query => single-pass streaming explanation (avg. 120 tokens).
- P95 latency requirement for production: 300ms TTFT.
- Peak TPS: 200 QPS sustained during peak windows; concurrency up to 80 during spikes.
- Streaming: prefer SSE to simplify browser integration, but WebSocket is acceptable if we need binary framing. Chunk cadence: ideally 150–300ms between chunks for UI smoothness.

What we’ll deliver next week:
1) A short TTFT benchmark plan (attached: ttft_test_plan.xlsx) with payloads, warm/cold run definitions, and expected measurement points.
2) Redwood appendix describing streaming options and recommended chunk thresholds (attached: redwood-ttft-appendix.pdf).
3) Proposed time for a technical deep-dive with Aditya to validate traces and measure a representative workload.

Ask from you: please confirm the payload sizes (avg and 95th token counts) for your queries and whether you insist on SSE vs WebSocket. If you can share a sample request/response trace (or synthetic payload), we can pre-run the bench and come prepared with results.

Proposed next meetings:
- Technical deep-dive with Aditya (45m): Tue, Mar 2 or Wed, Mar 3 — what works?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Looping in a couple of quick notes from the infra side so we can be targeted in the deep-dive:

1) TTFT definition — confirm we measure from request accept to first byte of model token (server-side) and include network RTT for client-observed SLO. We’ll report both server-only and client-observed P50/P95.

2) Warm vs cold — for your SLO we should focus on warm (steady-state KV cache primed) but include a cold-start health metric. Warm-state TTFT target: 300ms P95; cold-start budget: <1s P95.

3) Streaming cadence — recommendations: aim for chunk cadence 150–250ms for UI fluidity. Use a chunk token threshold of ~32–48 tokens OR 4KB payload threshold, whichever comes first. This keeps latency predictable while avoiding excessive small frames.

4) Concurrency and batching — at 200 QPS we expect batching to be beneficial for throughput but can increase TTFT if batch windows exceed 20–30ms. Recommend configuring dynamic batching with max wait 15ms and per-GPU batch size tuned to your model.

5) Measurements we need from BlinkHealth to pre-run bench: representative payloads (you mentioned median/95th above), 10 sample traces including request/response timestamps, and expected client network latency distribution (percentiles).

I attached a short checklist to the Drive folder Marissa linked — will pick a Tue/Mar 2 slot if Alex confirms.

—Aditya
